transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… I’ve just been waking up with this heavy sadness. Like everything’s there—the studio, the lights—but there’s no music in me anymore.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yeah… I think so. It kind of started after I hurt my ankle. It’s been… about two months now, this whole thing.
Do these feelings seem mainly connected to your ankle injury?
I think so, yeah. It sort of started after the ankle injury… and it’s been about two months like this.
Have these feelings made it hard for you to do your usual day-to-day activities?

Yeah… somewhat. I’m still doing the basic things, showing up when I have to, but I’m not really keeping up. I fell behind on teaching prep, missed a grant deadline… and my studio got messy enough that other people had to take over scheduling. It’s not like me.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know… not exactly. I still like some things, I think. It’s just been harder to really get into them lately.
Before this started after your ankle injury, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

Not really like this. What brought me in is… I’ve been waking up with this heavy, hollow sadness. Like the studio lights are on, but there’s no music in me anymore. I don’t remember having that for weeks before.
Have you been feeling especially worried or anxious a lot of the time since this started?
I don’t know… not a lot, I don’t think. I’ve been uneasy sometimes, but I wouldn’t say worried all the time.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
A little, maybe. It’s more like… I wake up and everything feels hollow. Like the lights are on, but there’s no music. It’s hard not to feel like it’ll stay that way.
Since this started, have you been feeling worthless?

Yeah… somewhat. I keep thinking about the performances that got cancelled and… telling myself I let everyone down. The dancers, the funders, the community. People have been kind about it, but it feels like more kindness than I deserve.
Since this started, has your sleep changed?

Yeah… it’s been pretty uneven. Some nights I’m up until almost morning sketching out formations, and lately I’ll crash from being exhausted but then wake up around four or five with my stomach all tight.
Since this started, have you been feeling down or sad most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… most days, I think. I’ve been waking up with this heavy, hollow sadness. Like… the studio lights are on, but there’s no music in me anymore.
Since this started, has your appetite changed?
Yeah… somewhat. When I was really buzzing with ideas, I’d just forget to eat. And now when I do, it kind of tastes like cardboard. My rehearsal clothes feel looser lately.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I’ve felt pretty low, but… I don’t think I want to get into anything more than that right now.
Since this started, have other people noticed that you’re moving or speaking more slowly than usual?
Yeah… I think so. I’ve noticed it too. Even just crossing the studio to get my notebook feels… slow. Like I’m moving through wet sand or something.
Since this started, have you been feeling nervous or on edge a lot of the time?
I’m not sure. Maybe a little tense sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been nervous all the time.
Since this started, have you had a period where you felt unusually energetic or revved up?

Yeah… there was a stretch where I felt kind of revved up. Even with the injury, I kept jumping from one thing to another—sketching maps, emailing people, reorganizing music files… like I had to redo the whole project all at once.
During that revved-up stretch, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… during that stretch, I didn’t seem to need much. I’d stay up sketching formations until it was basically morning. Lately it’s different—I crash, but then I’m awake at four or five with my stomach all tight.
During that revved-up stretch, did you feel unusually confident or powerful—like you could do things other people couldn't?

Yeah… I guess I did. I really thought I could turn all of this into this big, career-defining piece—something that would change how people saw dance and wilderness. And I remember being kind of stunned that other people weren’t immediately seeing it that way.
During that revved-up stretch, did it get severe enough that you had to be hospitalized?
No… I mean, not that it got to that point. I wasn’t hospitalized.
During that revved-up stretch, did it cause major problems in your life or work?

Yeah… it did. I was still showing up for the important things, but I fell behind on teaching prep, missed a grant deadline, and my studio was kind of a mess. People I work with started taking over basic scheduling because I wasn’t keeping up like I usually do.
